cards.explanation: The answer is: divide the inheritance with me. Someone in the crowd says, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me." (Luke 12:13) He asks Jesus to step in on an inheritance. Notice he's just someone in the crowd, and he asks Jesus straight out, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus doesn't agree to settle it. He answers, "Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?" (Luke 12:14) Then He moves on to something bigger, friends, which is how this whole teaching gets started.
The answer is greed. Jesus says, "Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed…" (Luke 12:15) Look at that word "every," friends. He isn't picking out one kind. He means all of them.

The answer is that life is not about how much you own. Jesus says, "…for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions." (Luke 12:15) You can own a LOT, friends, and that still isn't what your life is made of. It's the reason behind the warning.

The answer is store. The rich man thinks, "What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?" (Luke 12:17) The ground gave him an abundance, and now he's out of room. That's a problem I would LOVE to have, friends.

The plan is to tear down his barns and build bigger ones. He says, "I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods." (Luke 12:18) Notice who he's talking to, friends. It's all "I will" and "my."

The answer is True. The rich man plans to say to himself, "You have plenty of good things laid up for many years." (Luke 12:19) That's quite a pep talk, friends, and he's the only one in the audience. I bet it felt great while it lasted.

The answer is that his life will be required of him. God says, "This very night your life will be required of you." (Luke 12:20) Look at that timing, friends. He planned for many years, and God speaks about tonight.

The answer is True. God says, "Then who will own what you have accumulated?" (Luke 12:20) It's a question, friends, and the man gets no answer in the text. All those barns, and nobody named to get them.

The answer is God. Jesus says, "This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God." (Luke 12:21) That's the one thing the man left out, friends. Good work today, bakers.
